አደይ አበባ ነሽ ውብ አበባ

VERSE 1: 

You are my reliance for my life salvation
Look upon me do not give me to conviction

መመኪያዬ አንተ ነህ የነፍሴ መዳኛ

I will give my life (2) unto You
My Creator and Lord where should I look for You

ሕይወቴን ለአንተ (2) ብያለሁ

VERSE 2: 

Cleanse me of transgressions and from all of my sins

transliteration_title: You’re The Soul For My Soul English Orthodox Tewahedo Hymn
description:
Original Singer : Zemari Kesis Mindaye Berhanu
Original Song : Lenefese nefeswa nesh 

Mezmur translator:- Zemarit Gellila Yohannes

Lenefese nefeswa nesh, Lemengede fana
Endaltefa amnalew, Yanchi lij Negna

You’re the soul for my soul, and the Light of my path
I know I won’t perish i’m a child of Yours

Mothers of the righteous, in number they’re many
Before and after Christ, truly they are plenty
But Mary You are one, there is no one like You
You live on for ages, guiding us all to You

All those who call on you, all who honor your name
All who offer praises, your glory who proclaims
Truly he does profit, and truly does he gain
There is none who loses, there is none put to shame

Saint Gregory and the, righteous father St John
St Basil who is Great, and St. Athanasius 
Our teacher St. Ephrem and St George our father
All profited from you, calling you their Mother

Go and ask your Fathers, is what the Word proclaims
And when we did ask them, all of the righteous saints 
They did tell us of You, how you endlessly love
How you plead for mankind, saving us from above 

Gabriel from heaven, Elizabeth from Earth
Together they did preach, honor to Virgin birth 
Whoever pleads to You, calling upon Your name
He can only profit, no one is put to shame

The miracle of the birth of our great Lord
To announce the good news, the Angel descended.

This is a mystery, that cannot be expressed,
But in her heart Virgin Mary kept it guarded (2)

The wise men they arrived from the eastern nations

A Galilean king has come from Nazareth

I called unto my Dear Lord when my life was impaired 
I called unto my Father when I had none to spare
My anxiousness he calmed rescued me from despair 

When I appeal to Him He hears my desperate cry
His ears are attentive and open are His eyes
For He will rescue me from a life that is grim
I may be unworthy but still I will praise Him

Unable to walk on the path of righteousness 
The drowning waves of sin seemed to me tireless
When I appealed to Him with a regretful heart
He brought forth His mercy and pulled me from the dark

Just as you saved Noah rescue us from the storm
Shield us from the arrows coming in every form
My strength will be in you I won’t tremble in fear 
I will lean on the cross knowing my God is near 

With abundant mercy death was left in the past
He never left His child showing His love is vast
God received me with joy with His bright shining light
Who will stand against me with my Lord as my might

Nikodimos nikodemos kibur
Lelitun bebirehan yemimar memehir 
Nikodimos Nikodimos the honored
From dusk until dawn, A teacher who learns 

Despite the darkened sky, one star shined in the night
Neglecting worldly things, steadfast amid the plight
Though he was a teacher, he never ceased to learn
The tethers of his pride, with humbleness, he did tear and did spurn

A love that conquers fear, did reign within his heart
He buried his Teacher, through this he did his part
the Shroud of our Lord, he honored with perfume
In doing so he was given life with Christ the heavenly groom

Passing from Lord to lord, true Wisdom was revealed 
To those who keep the Law, I will advise indeed 
If your soul awakens, and returns from her sins 
Just like Nikodimos, your soul, stands with the Lord therein

description:
ክብሩ ከመላእክት ከፍ ከፍ ያለ ነው
የስሙ ትርጓሜ ማን እንደ እግዚአብሔር ነው
ሚካኤል ስለው ሚካኤል 
ያስጨነቀኝ ከቅጥሬ ሸሽቷል

የአፎሚያ ረዳት የባህራን አባት
እስራኤል ዘስጋን የመራቸው ከፊት 
ዛሬ አስምር ብለው ደጁ ለሚጠኑ
ከአምላክ የተሰጠው ፅኑ ናት ኪዳኑ
      ልክ እንደ ትናንቱ የምትጠብቀኝ 
      በበጉ ዙፋን ፊት የምትቆምልኝ 

መንገድ ለጠፋው ሰው ለሚቅበዘበዘው
አንገቱን በሐዘን ለሚወዘውዘው 
ምልጃህ ነው የረዳው ጌታ ፊት መቆምህ 
ለእኔም መልስ ሆነሃል ሚካኤል ሆይ ስልህ 
      ልክ እንደ ትናንቱ የምትጠብቀኝ 
      በበጉ ዙፋን ፊት የምትቆምልኝ 

ስምህክን እየጠራሁ ደጅህ አድጌያለሁ
ምልጃህ እያገዘኝ ስንቱን አልፌለሁ 
ለሰው ማይነገር ላንተ የነገሬህ
ችግሬ ተፈቷል በፊቴ ቀድመህ 
     ልክ እንደ ትናንቱ የምትጠብቀኝ 
     በበጉ ዙፋን ፊት የምትቆምልኝ 

የመዳንን መንገድ መንግስቱን እንድወርስ
ስደክም ያገዝከኝ  ቀርበኸኝ  በሞገስ
ሃይላት ስልጣናትን መናፍቱን ረትተህ 
በሰማይ አልፈሃል ሚካኤል ድንቅ ነህ 
     ልክ እንደ ትናንቱ የምትጠብቀኝ 
     በበጉ ዙፋን ፊት የምትቆምልኝ

description:
Alemu Aga was born in 1950 in Entoto, near Addis Ababa. He has played the Ethiopian traditional lyre Begenna since he was 12, having been trained by a famous master, Aleqa Alemayehu Wolde-Ammanuel, who was his neighbour and teacher at his school.

After graduating from the Addis Ababa University (with a degree in geography), he taught the Begenna at the Yared Music School until 1980.

He now teaches on a voluntary basis and focuses on his research about the Begenna.

Alemu has published numerous audiotapes and several CD's and appeared in concert worldwide. Nowadays, he is the most highly respected Begenna player of Ethiopia.

Title: „The Begenna of Elders\" (The Harp of David in Ethiopia)
Label: Laika Records
Time: 49:41 
CD / Digipak +booklet, 2009
Cat No: 3510255.2

To download the CD go to: http://itunes.apple.com/us/album/the-...


„Alemu Aga ist der heute wichtigste Begenna-Interpret in Äthiopien.\"

Geboren 1950 in Addis Abeba, begann er mit zwölf Jahren seine Ausbildung in der seltenen Kunst des Spiels auf der Davidsharfe, der Begenna. Bereits zehn Jahre später nahm die UNESCO eine LP mit traditioneller Musik aus Äthiopien auf, auf der er die Begenna spielte.

Das Instrument ist seit wenigen Jahren wieder ins kulturelle Leben der christlichen Äthiopier zurückgekehrt, die Musik der Davidsharfe ist vor allem während der Fastenzeiten zu hören. Die Begenna selbst soll - dem Glauben der Äthiopier nach - von Gott auf die Erde zu König David gebracht worden sein, damit dieser ihn mit frommen Liedern preise. Bauweise und Stimmung haben sich seit biblischen Zeiten nicht geändert.

Nach wie vor darf die Begenna nicht gleichzeitig mit anderen Musikinstrumenten erklingen, nicht einmal mit den kirchlichen Instrumenten, dem Sistrum, der Kebero und dem Gebetsstock.

ይችን ዓመት ተወኝ 
ከዓመት እስከአመት ፍሬን ሳላፈራ ደረቅ እንደሆንኩኞ

በራድ ወይም ትኩስ ሁለቱንም ሳልሆን እንዲያው ለብ እንዳልኩኝ ፤
አለሁኝ በቤትህ ለሙን መሬትህን እያጎሳቆልኩኝ ፤

አውቃለሁ አምላኬ ፍሬየን ለመልቀም እንዳመላለስኩህ ፤
ዛሬም ሳላፈራ እሾህን አብቅየ  ደርቄ ጠበኩህ  ፤

ያልተደረገልኝ ያላፈሰስክብኝ ያልሰጠኸኝ የለም ፤
ነገር ግን ይህ ሁሉ አላርምህ አለኝ አልለየኝም ከአለም ።
የማትሰለቸኝ ሆይ ተነስቼ እስክቆም እባክህ ታገሰኝ ፤
የኔን ክፋት ተወዉ መልአክህን ሰምተህ ይችን ዓመት ተወኝ ። 

  አውቃለሁ ታውቃለህ ቀጠሮን ሰጥቼ እንደማላከብር፤
ብዙ ግዜ አቅጄ ብዙ ጊዜ ዝቼ በወሬ እንደምቀር ።

ዘንድሮስ እንዳልኩኝ አምና ይኸ  ጊዜ ሰምተኸኝ ነበረ፤
ምንም ሳልለወጥ ዘንድሮየ አልፎ ባዲስ ተቀየረ  ።

ፍሬ የማይወጣኝ እኔን በመኮትኮት እጆችህ ደከሙ ፤
እኔ ግን አለሁኝ ዛሬም አልበቃኝም በኃጢአት መታመሙ ።

የቃልህን ውሐ በድንጋይ ልጅህ ላይ  ሳትታክት ስታፈስ ዘመን ተቆጠረ ፤
ወደልቤ ሳይሰርግ ህይወቴን ሳይለውጥ እንዲያው ፈስሶ ቀረ ።

ቃልህን ጠግቤ እያገሳሁት ነው ሌሎች እስኪሰሙ ፤
በቃልህ መኖር ግን አልያዝህ አለኝ ከበደኝ ቀለሙ ።

ብዙ ጥቅስ አገኝሁ  ከቅዱስ መጽሐፍህ ገልጬ አይቼ ፤
ከራሴ ላይ ብቻ አንድ ጥቅስ አጣሁንኝ  በበደል ተኝቼ  ።
ውጤቴ ደካማ ትምህርት የማይሰርጸኝ  ተማሪ ብሆንም ፤
ይችን ዓመት ተወኝ ተደግሞ ትንሽ ልማር ታገሰኝ አሁንም  ።

እባክህ አልቆረጥ በቅዱስ መሬትህ  ልቆይ ፍቀድልኝ ፤
ያፈሩት ቅዱሳን የፍሬያቸው ሽታ መአዛ እንዲደርሰኝ ።

የተሸከምከኝ ሆይ ዛሬም ተሸከመኝ አትሰልቸኝ አደራ ፤
ማን ይታገሰኛል ጠላት እየሆንኩት   እየሰሩ ስሰራ ።

አታውጣኝ ከቤትህ ብዙ ቦታ አልይዝም ፍሬ ስለሌለኝ
ስፍራ የማያሻኝ  ቤት የማላጣብብ ፍሬ አልባ በለስ ነኝ ።

ቦታ የሚይዙት ባለምግባሮቹ ቅዱሳንህ ናቸው ፤
ልክ እንደዘንባባ የተንዠረገገ ተጋድሎ ጽድቃቸው ።
ከሊባኖስ ዝግባ  እጅጉን የበዛ  ገድል ትሩፋታቸው ፤

እኔ አይደለሁም ቦታስ የምትይዘው የአንተው እናት ናት ፤
ስሮቿ በምድር  ጫፎቿ በሰማይ ሲደርሱ ያየናት  ፤
ይችን አመት ተወኝ  ከስሯ እሆናለሁ ባፈራ ምናልባት ፤

ይቺን ዓመት ተወኝ እባክህ አምላኬ አንድ ዓመት ምንህ ናት ፤
ሺህ ዓመት አንድ ቀን አይደለም ወይ ላንተ ዓመት ኢምንትህ ናት ።

ይኸ ዓመት አልፎ ደግሞ ዓመት ስጠኝ እስከምልህ ድረስ  ፤
እባክህ ጌታየ ይችን ዓመት ተወኝ  የወጉን እንዳደርስ ።

ALEMU AGA - the famous Begenna Player from Ethiopia


Alemu Aga was born in 1950 in Entoto, near Addis Ababa. He has played the Ethiopian traditional lyre Begenna since he was 12, having been trained by a famous master, Aleqa Alemayehu Wolde-Ammanuel, who was his neighbour and teacher at his school.

After graduating from the Addis Ababa University (with a degree in geography), he taught the Begenna at the Yared Music School until 1980. He now teaches on a voluntary basis and focuses on his research about the Begenna.

Alemu has published numerous audiotapes and several CD's and appeared in concert worldwide. Nowadays, he is the most highly respected Begenna player of Ethiopia.

„Alemu Aga ist der heute wichtigste Begenna-Interpret in Äthiopien.\"

Geboren 1950 in Addis Abeba, begann er mit zwölf Jahren seine Ausbildung in der seltenen Kunst des Spiels auf der Davidsharfe, der Begenna. Bereits zehn Jahre später nahm die UNESCO eine LP mit traditioneller Musik aus Äthiopien auf, auf der er die Begenna spielte.
Das Instrument ist seit wenigen Jahren wieder ins kulturelle Leben der christlichen Äthiopier zurückgekehrt, die Musik der Davidsharfe ist vor allem während der Fastenzeiten zu hören. Die Begenna selbst soll - dem Glauben der Äthiopier nach - von Gott auf die Erde zu König David gebracht worden sein, damit dieser ihn mit frommen Liedern preise. Bauweise und Stimmung haben sich seit biblischen Zeiten nicht geändert. Nach wie vor darf die Begenna nicht gleichzeitig mit anderen Musikinstrumenten erklingen, nicht einmal mit den kirchlichen Instrumenten, dem Sistrum, der Kebero und dem Gebetsstock.

This group is a platform for young adults to ask questions, join discussions and network with fellow brothers and sister of the Orthodox Tewahedo faith. We all know as high school draws to an end or as we start experiencing the freedoms of college we tend to astray from our spiritual life. It can be difficult finding an Orthodox Tewahedo church nearby or finding a way to balance out our spiritual and normal life. Discover the Begena:
The Ancient Ethiopian Harp 

Welcome to our dedicated space for the Begena, a remarkable traditional Ethiopian instrument that has been captivating hearts for centuries. Known as the \"Harp of David,\" the Begena is not just a musical instrument; it is a vessel of spiritual depth and cultural heritage, echoing the rich traditions of Ethiopia. 

What is the Begena? 

The Begena is a large, ten-stringed lyre that produces deep, resonant tones, often used in spiritual and meditative music. Its unique, calming sound is attributed to its construction, which includes a large, box-like resonator covered in animal skin. The instrument is traditionally played with a plectrum made of horn, producing its distinctive, buzzing timbre 

Historical Significance 

Rooted in ancient Ethiopian history, the Begena is believed to have connections to King David of the Bible, who played the harp. For centuries, it has been a symbol of tranquility and devotion, often played during times of reflection or religious observance. The Begena is more than just an instrument; it is a link to the spiritual practices and historical narratives of Ethiopia.

This group is a platform for young adults to ask questions, join discussions and network with fellow brothers and sister of the Orthodox Tewahedo faith. We all know as high school draws to an end or as we start experiencing the freedoms of college we tend to astray from our spiritual life. It can be difficult finding an Orthodox Tewahedo church nearby or finding a way to balance out our spiritual and normal life. That’s why it’s essential to have people to network with that have passed or are currently in the same situation, have the same questions and/or are just looking for some guides. transliteration_title: You Triumph the Works of Evil
description:
Original Song: Hayal Neh Ante
Singer: Liqe Mezemeran Tewodros Yosef

You triumph the works of evil
The mighty angel St. Gebriel
Let the enemy surrender 
Be my rescuing defender

ኃያል ነህ አንተ ኃያል
ደጉ መልአክ ገብርኤል
ይውደቅ ይሸነፍ ጠላት
አንተ ተራዳን በውነት

On the field of Dura 
An idol was arranged 
To favor its worship
A law had been proclaimed
But the wise children had remained faithful and true
They turned to The Most High temptations they subdued 

Frustrated was the king
With the youthful children 
In fire to be burned
He ordered to throw them
Descended down from the heavens as he was sent 
Untouched by the fire he saved them from torment 

They were filled with praises
Beneath the fire pit
The ones that pushed them in
Found themselves within it
They persevered with joy aided by Almighty
The nobles of the king witnessed the Lord’s glory 

Nebuchadnezzar was
Bemused by what he saw
The mighty arch angel
Snatched them out of his claw 
He praised the Lord who sent the angel to save them
He kneeled before their God for worship unto Him

The Ancient Ethiopian Harp 

Welcome to our dedicated space for the Begena, a remarkable traditional Ethiopian instrument that has been captivating hearts for centuries. Known as the \"Harp of David,\" the Begena is not just a musical instrument; it is a vessel of spiritual depth and cultural heritage, echoing the rich traditions of Ethiopia. 

What is the Begena? 

The Begena is a large, ten-stringed lyre that produces deep, resonant tones, often used in spiritual and meditative music. Its unique, calming sound is attributed to its construction, which includes a large, box-like resonator covered in animal skin. The instrument is traditionally played with a plectrum made of horn, producing its distinctive, buzzing timbre 

Historical Significance 

Rooted in ancient Ethiopian history, the Begena is believed to have connections to King David of the Bible, who played the harp. For centuries, it has been a symbol of tranquility and devotion, often played during times of reflection or religious observance. The Begena is more than just an instrument; it is a link to the spiritual practices and historical narratives of Ethiopia.

transliteration_title: Alemu Aga from Ethiopia playing the Begenna
description:
Alemu Aga was born in 1950 in Entoto, near Addis Ababa. He has played the Ethiopian traditional lyre Begenna since he was 12, having been trained by a famous master, Aleqa Alemayehu Wolde-Ammanuel, who was his neighbour and teacher at his school.

After graduating from the Addis Ababa University (with a degree in geography), he taught the Begenna at the Yared Music School until 1980.

He now teaches on a voluntary basis and focuses on his research about the Begenna.

Alemu has published numerous audiotapes and several CD's and appeared in concert worldwide. Nowadays, he is the most highly respected Begenna player of Ethiopia.

„Alemu Aga ist der heute wichtigste Begenna-Interpret in Äthiopien.\"

Geboren 1950 in Addis Abeba, begann er mit zwölf Jahren seine Ausbildung in der seltenen Kunst des Spiels auf der Davidsharfe, der Begenna. Bereits zehn Jahre später nahm die UNESCO eine LP mit traditioneller Musik aus Äthiopien auf, auf der er die Begenna spielte.

Das Instrument ist seit wenigen Jahren wieder ins kulturelle Leben der christlichen Äthiopier zurückgekehrt, die Musik der Davidsharfe ist vor allem während der Fastenzeiten zu hören. Die Begenna selbst soll - dem Glauben der Äthiopier nach - von Gott auf die Erde zu König David gebracht worden sein, damit dieser ihn mit frommen Liedern preise. Bauweise und Stimmung haben sich seit biblischen Zeiten nicht geändert.

Nach wie vor darf die Begenna nicht gleichzeitig mit anderen Musikinstrumenten erklingen, nicht einmal mit den kirchlichen Instrumenten, dem Sistrum, der Kebero und dem Gebetsstock.
